question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Governance practices of European powers in Indian territories]
options: Portuguese Goa – Introduced the Inquisition to enforce Catholic Christianity among converts
English EIC – Adopted a policy of non-interference in local customs and religion in early years
Dutch VOC at Pulicat – Promoted conversion to Dutch Reformed Protestantism among the local population
French Pondicherry – Allowed Jesuits and other missionaries to operate but avoided forced conversion policies
wrong_fact: The Dutch VOC was primarily a commercial enterprise and did NOT actively promote religious conversion among Indian populations at Pulicat or elsewhere in India. Unlike the Portuguese who aggressively pursued Christianization, the VOC was officially Protestant but focused on trade, not missionary activity. The Dutch Reformed Church operated among Dutch settlers, not as a conversion tool for Indians.
explanation: The Portuguese in Goa enforced Catholicism through the Inquisition (1560–1812), destroying Hindu temples and coercing converts. The early English EIC followed a deliberate non-interference policy in Indian religious matters. The French allowed Catholic missions (Jesuits were active in Pondicherry) but without the coercive measures of the Portuguese. The Dutch VOC, however, was a secular commercial body — it did not promote religious conversion among Indians at Pulicat or elsewhere.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [British governance practices and their geographic application]
options: Cornwallis Reforms (1793) – Introduced Civil Services merit system; Indians excluded from positions above Rs. 500 p.a.
Munro's Ryotwari Settlement – Applied in Madras Presidency; promoted direct state-peasant relationship
Dalhousie's Railways – First railway line from Bombay to Thane (1853); primarily for military and commercial purposes
Macaulay's Minute on Education (1835) – Promoted vernacular education and recommended Sanskrit and Arabic as medium of instruction
wrong_fact: Macaulay's Minute on Education (1835) was the EXACT OPPOSITE — it recommended English as the medium of instruction and dismissed Sanskrit and Arabic as inferior for modern education. Macaulay famously wrote that 'a single shelf of a good European library was worth the whole native literature of India.' He advocated English-medium education to create Indians who were 'Indian in blood and colour, but English in taste.'
explanation: Cornwallis's reforms (1793) indeed barred Indians from civil posts above Rs. 500 per annum salary. Munro's Ryotwari system (from 1820) created a direct revenue relationship between the state and cultivating ryots in Madras. The first railway in India ran from Bombay (Bori Bunder) to Thane on April 16, 1853. Macaulay's Minute (1835) championed English education, NOT vernacular education — option D is completely wrong.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Governance practices – Treaties, alliances, and subsidiary forces across regions]
options: Treaty of Allahabad (1765) – Established EIC's Diwani rights over Bengal, Bihar, Orissa; Shah Alam II received annual tribute from EIC
Subsidiary Alliance with Hyderabad (1798) – First formal Subsidiary Alliance under Wellesley; Nizam paid for British troops
Treaty of Bassein (1802) – Peshwa Baji Rao II accepted British protection; triggered Second Anglo-Maratha War
Treaty of Srirangapatnam (1792) – Ended the Third Anglo-Mysore War; Tipu Sultan ceded Malabar to EIC and Daman to Portuguese
wrong_fact: The Treaty of Srirangapatnam (1792) ended the Third Anglo-Mysore War and required Tipu Sultan to cede half his kingdom, pay Rs. 3.3 crore war indemnity, and hand over two of his sons as hostages. Malabar was ceded to the EIC — this part is correct. However, 'Daman to Portuguese' is entirely fabricated. Daman was already under Portuguese control and was never part of Mysore's territories ceded in 1792.
explanation: The Treaty of Allahabad (1765) gave EIC the Diwani with Shah Alam II receiving Rs. 26 lakh annually and Allahabad-Kara districts. The Subsidiary Alliance with Hyderabad (1798) was Wellesley's first. The Treaty of Bassein (1802) with Peshwa Baji Rao II indeed triggered the Second Anglo-Maratha War (1803–05). The Treaty of Srirangapatnam (1792) had Tipu cede Malabar, Dindigul, Baramahal to EIC and territories to Marathas and Nizam — no Portuguese connection at all.
